newsitem.title: UK: NWE low sulphur fuel oil crumbles under supply.
newsitem.headline: NWE low sulphur fuel oil crumbles under supply.

text.p: NWE low sulphur cracked fuel oil prices fell sharply again on Wednesday as prompt supply blossomed, prompting the emergence of some fresh buying interest, traders said.
Offers were seen as low as $127 cif Italy for early February delivery, but even this number failed to ignite Italian interest.
An NWE refiner was heard having sold a low sulphur cargo to another NWE refiner at $124.50 cif Med. With freight at around $10 a tonne, this was equivalent to only a dollar or two below swaps.
A Spanish refiner was heard buying a low sulphur ex-U.K. cargo on Tuesday at the quoted cif high +$1, cif Tenerife.
A French refiner also bought 20,000 tonnes of low sulphur fuel oil in a tender. The seller was thought to be a French refiner and the price was not thought to be representative of the market.
High sulphur fuel oil held its ground better but took a hit from falling low sulphur values.
Barges traded in the morning at $119 then slipped progressively through the day to trade at $116. A 25,000 tonne cargo, loading January 14-19, was heard sold to an NWE refiner at $110.50 fob NWE.
Bunker supply was improving. One potential buyer for the Med said he saw at least four cargoes, two of which were sourced out of NWE.
